description: Classify the release impact of one merged pull request.

params.pr: Pull request metadata and either the complete unified diff, one complete-file chunk, or a whole-PR synthesis of all chunk analyses. Fields include title, description, labels, changed file paths, URL, diff content, and diff_truncated flag. Chunked requests include chunk_index, chunk_count, and analysis_mode=complete-file-chunk. Synthesis requests use analysis_mode=chunk-aggregate, an intentionally empty diff, and chunk_results containing each chunk classification, confidence, and analysis. On a second-pass request, review_pass=true and initial_analysis contain the prior classification response.

impact.instructions: Choose the single highest user-facing release impact of this merged pull request. Analyze the actual code diff first, using the title, description, labels, and changed file paths as supporting context. Cite concrete changed behavior from the diff in your reasoning. Do not infer a feature from implementation-only work. If review_pass=true, independently reassess the diff and initial_analysis, explicitly address why the first classification was uncertain, and correct it when the evidence supports a clearer answer. If diff_truncated is true, the diff is empty, binary-only, Jev cannot process the complete diff, or evidence is insufficient, choose review. Choose major only when a breaking change is explicitly evidenced; choose minor only for an evidenced additive user-facing capability. If uncertainty is only whether a compatible maintenance change warrants a patch or no release, prefer patch when a user-facing fix/reliability/performance improvement is evidenced, otherwise none. Choose review when ambiguity could plausibly change the outcome to major/minor, when compatibility risk is unresolved, or when the diff does not support a reliable decision. For analysis_mode=complete-file-chunk, classify only the potential impact evidenced by this chunk, while using PR metadata as context; do not assume unseen chunks are unchanged. A chunk that cannot be assessed independently, suggests cross-file compatibility risk, or lacks enough evidence must be review. For analysis_mode=chunk-aggregate, the empty diff is intentional: synthesize the overall PR impact from the title, description, changed file paths, and every entry in chunk_results. Reconcile the chunk analyses in the context of the whole feature; do not treat each chunk as an independent PR or simply choose the highest-confidence chunk. Acknowledge cross-file behavior and any disagreement. Choose major/minor only when the aggregate evidence supports it; choose patch/none only when the aggregate supports that distinction; otherwise choose review. On review_pass=true, reassess the aggregate and initial_analysis together. The caller requires confidence to meet the configured threshold after this synthesis. For dependency-update PRs, use upstream release notes in the PR description as evidence even when the repository diff contains only lockfiles. If the updated dependency is used by a shipped/public-facing surface (including the public developer documentation or API reference) and release notes explicitly describe a user-visible rendering, styling, correctness, reliability, or performance fix, classify it as patch when compatibility risk is not evidenced; do not choose review solely because implementation files are absent from this repository diff. Treat lint/formatting-only or build-tool-only changes as none when no user-facing effect is evidenced.

criteria.major: A change that breaks compatibility for existing users, configuration, data, APIs, or supported workflows. Choose only when a breaking change is explicitly evidenced.
criteria.minor: A new user-facing capability or meaningful additive behavior that remains backward-compatible and is evidenced by the diff.
criteria.patch: A user-facing bug fix, reliability improvement, performance improvement, or compatible maintenance change worth shipping, evidenced by the diff.
criteria.none: Documentation-only, tests-only, CI/release-automation-only, dependency or internal changes with no meaningful user-facing impact. Do not use none if the diff demonstrates a user-facing fix.
criteria.review: The diff is truncated or incomplete, empty, binary-only, Jev cannot process the complete diff, or evidence is ambiguous in a way that could materially affect major/minor classification or compatibility safety.
